scenes.vo: Every coal plant in India needs government permission. And every permission is public.
Public, like this. Two hundred and forty-six pages. Six hundred thousand characters.
Page eighteen. A thirteen-hundred-megawatt coal plant on the Hasdeo River skips its public hearing. Page twenty-five. Approved.
Nobody objected. Because nobody could read it.
So I built Vakeel. An AI advocate for the people next door.
Drop in any filing from the government portal.
Step Functions splits it into projects, and an Amazon Bedrock agent reads each one, in parallel.
Two hundred and forty-six pages. Fifty-two seconds.
But AI makes things up. So every number needs a word-for-word quote and a page, and code checks it against the PDF.
No quote, no claim. Sixty-five claims thrown out. Two hundred and nineteen survived.
What survives becomes plain language. In English. In Hindi. In Odia.
Then code, not the AI, does the math. Six point eight million tonnes of carbon a year. Water for almost eight lakh people, every day.
And every number opens the exact page it came from.
Search your district. See what's being approved near you.
Then, act. Vakeel drafts a formal objection from the committee's own record.
But it can't send a thing until you sign it. Step Functions waits for a human. Up to seven days.
All serverless, on AWS. Bedrock, Step Functions, Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, CloudFront, and Amazon Location. With a hard daily budget cap.
Three real filings. Seven hundred and thirty-two pages. Seventeen projects. Every claim checked.
Coal power in India is linked to as many as a hundred and fifteen thousand early deaths a year. The clearance file is the last place anyone can say no.
Vakeel makes sure the people who'll breathe it can read it first.
